messages:
anya: Heads-upI pushed a docs PR to tidy the provisioning migration guide and SLA table (https://github.com/redwood/inference-docs/pull/4689). Main asks: 1) fix two broken internal links, 2) add a tiny mapping table for old->new policy fields, and 3) tighten SLA phrasing around burst pools. Can folks quick-review?

sam: On it. Where are the broken links?

anya: The eviction-model link and the autoscale schema doc both 404 inside the guide. I found the correct targets in the handbook repo and added comments in the PR.

marta: Reading the mapping table now. Suggest we show a one-row example mapping old YAML -> new YAML for readability (very short).

kevin: I'll add an SDK snippet showing how to migrate an existing tenant policy programmatically: small snippet using python client. Keeping it 3 lines.

oliver: Quick copy note for SLA table: change "best-effort latency" to "no latency SLA" for burst pools. That wording avoids confusion in sales/discussions.

sam: +1 to the wording change. Also suggest a short changelog bullet: "Schema rename: threshold_pct -> target_utilization_pct". Helps users searching commit history.

anya: Good. Marta can you draft the YAML one-row example? Something like: `old: threshold_pct: 80\nnew: target_utilization_pct: 80` but formatted as inline YAML.

marta: Pushed a tiny table row and an inline YAML example. Also added a single-line note: "Burst pools are preemptible; do not rely on latency guarantees." with link to eviction-model.

kevin: SDK snippet added in the PR description: `client.update_policy(tenant_id=\"team-river\", policy={\"target_utilization_pct\":80, \"cooldown_seconds\":300})` - kept to one line per style guide.

docs-bot: Style checklist: examples <= 15 lines, use present tense, include param links. :white_check_mark:

anya: Thanks everyone. Once CI passes I'll squash & merge. If anyone wants a follow-up note for the migration email to customers, DM me and I'll draft it.
